facts.fact: two thick braids of very red hair
facts.quote: two braids of very thick, decidedly red hair

facts.fact: small freckled face with eyes that look green or gray depending on the light
facts.quote: her eyes, which looked green in some lights and moods and gray in others

facts.fact: vivid, romantic imagination that colors everything she sees
facts.quote: There was more scope for imagination

facts.fact: prone to dramatic, sweeping despair over small setbacks
facts.quote: in the depths of despair

facts.fact: orphan; her parents Walter and Bertha Shirley, both teachers, died of fever when she was an infant
facts.quote: She died of fever when I was just three months old.

facts.fact: saves Minnie May Barry from croup using nursing know-how learned from the Hammond twins
facts.quote: I know exactly what to do for croup.

facts.fact: talks torrentially and admits herself that she talks too much
facts.quote: People are always telling me I do.

facts.fact: swears an oath of eternal 'bosom friend' loyalty with Diana Barry
facts.quote: I solemnly swear to be faithful to my bosom friend, Diana Barry, as long as the sun and moon shall endure.

facts.fact: by the end of the book her hair is called auburn and her freckles have mostly faded
facts.quote: people are nice enough to tell me my hair is auburn now

facts.fact: has a quick, fiery temper
facts.quote: Did anybody ever see such a temper!

facts.fact: stubborn and strong-willed once she makes up her mind
facts.quote: I can _stop_ when I make up my mind to it

facts.fact: before Green Gables she was passed between Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Hammond's households and finally sent to the orphan asylum at Hopeton
facts.quote: I had to go to the asylum at Hopeton, because nobody would take me.

facts.fact: wins a First Class teaching license and the Avery scholarship at Queen's Academy
facts.quote: To take First Class License in one year and win the Avery scholarship

facts.fact: gives up going to Redmond College to stay home and teach after Marilla's eyesight begins failing
facts.quote: Anne Shirley had given up the idea of going to college and intended to stay home and teach

facts.fact: accidentally dyes her hair green with a peddler's dye she believed would turn it raven black
facts.quote: I dyed it.

facts.fact: breaks her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head after he calls her 'carrots'
facts.quote: and cracked it--slate not head--clear across.

facts.fact: her years-long feud with Gilbert Blythe, who mocked her red hair, ends in friendship
facts.quote: We are going to be the best of friends

antiFacts.why: her eyes are described as green or gray depending on light, never blue
her hair is famously red (later called auburn), not golden or blonde
Anne is established as relentlessly talkative and dramatic, not shy or quiet
she is a penniless orphan raised in poverty before being adopted

antiFacts.claim: marries Gilbert Blythe in this book
antiFacts.why: the book ends with them merely becoming friends again after years of feuding, not marrying

facts.fact: tall, thin, angular woman with dark, gray-streaked hair twisted into a hard knot
facts.quote: Marilla was a tall, thin woman, with angles and without curves

facts.fact: narrow experience and rigid conscience, though with a hidden sense of humor
facts.quote: She looked like a woman of narrow experience and rigid conscience, which she was

facts.fact: no-nonsense and impatient with Anne's imaginings, insists on plain facts
facts.quote: Just you stick to bald facts. Begin at the beginning.

facts.fact: an unmarried 'old maid' who has never before raised a child
facts.quote: Perhaps an old maid

facts.fact: decides, despite having never raised a child, to keep Anne rather than send her to the harsh Mrs. Blewett
facts.quote: never brought up a child, especially a girl, and I dare say

facts.fact: eventually declares outright that she loves Anne as her own flesh and blood
facts.quote: I love you as dear as if you were my own flesh and blood

facts.fact: speaks in short, dry, sharp retorts
facts.quote: Unromantic fiddlesticks!

facts.fact: her eyesight fails later in the book, risking total blindness
facts.quote: Blind! Anne, just think of it!

facts.fact: softens noticeably over the course of the book, becoming warmer and less crisp
facts.quote: Marilla Cuthbert has got _mellow_.

facts.fact: as a young woman she was informally courted by John Blythe, Gilbert's father, but quarreled with him and never married
facts.quote: People called him my beau.

facts.fact: considers selling Green Gables after Matthew's death and the bank failure, until Anne intervenes
facts.quote: He heard that I was going to sell Green Gables and he wants to buy it.

facts.fact: disciplines Anne by making her apologize to Mrs. Rachel Lynde for her temper
facts.quote: you must go to her and tell her you are very sorry for your bad temper and ask her to forgive you.

facts.fact: is Matthew's sister and runs the Green Gables household with him
facts.quote: always been such a good, kind brother to me

facts.fact: capable of a rare, reluctant smile that softens her grim exterior
facts.quote: Something like a reluctant smile, rather rusty from long disuse, mellowed

antiFacts.claim: warm and openly affectionate from the very start
antiFacts.why: Marilla is established as stern and undemonstrative, only softening gradually over the book

antiFacts.claim: Anne's biological aunt or blood relative
antiFacts.why: she and Matthew adopt Anne from an orphan asylum; there is no blood relation
Matthew is her brother, not her husband; she is called an unmarried 'old maid'
she is repeatedly described as an aging, graying 'old maid,' not young
her hair is dark with gray streaks, worn in a hard knot, not red or curly

facts.fact: odd-looking, ungainly figure with long iron-gray hair and a full soft brown beard
facts.quote: an odd-looking personage, with an ungainly figure and long iron-gray hair that touched his stooping shoulders

facts.fact: the shyest man alive, dreads strangers and especially women
facts.quote: he was the shyest man alive and hated to have to go among strangers or to any place where he might have to talk.

facts.fact: quiet and silent, like his own father before him
facts.quote: shy and silent as his son after him

facts.fact: a farmer who lives at Green Gables in Avonlea with his sister Marilla
facts.quote: Green Gables was built at the furthest edge of his cleared land

facts.fact: secretly arranges through Mrs. Lynde to buy Anne a dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas
facts.quote: a Christmas present for you, Anne

facts.fact: his catchphrase is a hesitant 'Well now'
facts.quote: Well now, I dunno

facts.fact: brother to Marilla; the two of them run Green Gables together
facts.quote: Matthew dreaded all women except Marilla and Mrs. Rachel

facts.fact: looked much the same at sixty as he did at twenty
facts.quote: he had looked at twenty very much as he looked at sixty, lacking a little of the grayness.

facts.fact: quietly advocates to keep Anne despite Marilla's objections, and is proud of her later achievements
facts.quote: We might be some good to her

facts.fact: an old bachelor who never married
facts.quote: but I guess she knows more than an old bachelor.

facts.fact: dies of a sudden heart shock after reading news of a bank failure
facts.quote: before they could reach him Matthew had fallen across the threshold.

facts.fact: speaks haltingly and shyly, often stammering
facts.quote: I--I thought it might come in handy sometime

facts.fact: enjoys and defends Anne's talkativeness to Marilla from their very first meeting
facts.quote: You should have heard her talk coming from the station.

facts.fact: proud of Anne's academic success, calling her 'my girl'
facts.quote: It was a girl--my girl--my girl

antiFacts.why: Matthew is repeatedly described as the shyest man alive who dreads talking to strangers
he is her adoptive guardian; her biological father was Walter Shirley, who died when she was an infant
he is called an old bachelor who never married
he is an elderly man, described as looking much the same at sixty as at twenty
he has a full, soft brown beard worn since he was twenty
